title: CRE FORM 2
text:
CRE FORM TWO MARKING SCHEME
  (a) Bible as God’s word
  Bible authors wrote under influence of the Holy Spirit
  God is the author of the Bible. Wrote the ten laws
  Contains true message of God for daily living
  Deals with God’s revelation to human beings
  Talks about God’s nature
  Talks about Jesus Christ God’s son
  Has prophecies which came to pass
  Has words of prophets who were God’s messengers
 (b) Similarities in creation stories
  Both male and female were created
  Both God is the sole creator
  Both marriage was God ordained
  Both man was given responsibility
  Both everything created was for man’s benefit
  Both man is portrayed as superior to other creatures
  Both God is the source of life
 (c) Conditions for the renewal of Sinai Covenant
  Not to intermarry with foreigners.
  To keep the Sabbath day holy
  To keep the feast of the Passover
  Not to worship any idol gods
  Not to make treaties with other notices
  To obey God’s commandments
  To breakdown altars of idols in Canaan
  Dedicate their first born sons as well as those of their domestic slaves to
 God.
 2 (a) David greatest Israel King
  He honoured and obeyed God
  Established a strong military army
  Captured Jerusalem from Jebusites
  Established good international relations with neighboring states
  Improved economic status of Israel through trade.
  He expanded territorial boundaries of Israel
  He was chosen by god
  He had outstanding leadership qualities
  He composed psalms used in worship
  He consulted and obeyed God’s servants
 (b) Relevancy of Elijah’s prophetic mission to Christians
  Christians should be ready to perform the tasks given to them by God.
  Christians should obey God’s commandments to avoid judgement.
  Should condemn and avoid idolatry
  Should defend/ advocate for the rights of the poor and disadvantaged
  Should remain faithful to God when faced with challenges.
  We should be prayerful, have faith and patience.
 (c) How TAS related to the living dead
  Naming children after them
  Maintaining their graves
  Giving the dead a decent burial
  Pouring libations daily
  Inviting them to participate in communal activities
  Communicating with them through mediums
  Offering sacrifices to them
 3 (a) Jeremiah’s prophecies concerning the messiah
  The messiah will be a descendant of David
  The Messiah will rule wisely
  He will do what is just and right
  He will save Judah
  Israel will be safe during His time
  His name will be the Lord our righteousness
 (b) Ways in which John the Baptist prepared way
  He baptized Jesus
  He advised people to live a holy life
  He preached repentance of sins
  He acknowledged Jesus’ greatness
  He introduced Jesus to the people
  He handed his disciples to Jesus
  He baptized repentant sinners
 (c) Lessons Christians learn from the Magnificant
  God is holy
  He is merciful
  Powerful
  He is just
  He uplifts the lowly
  God keeps the promises
  God is a source of blessing
  God is helper to His servant Israel
 (d) Why Jesus was rejected in Nazareth
  He claimed that Isaiah’s prophecy had been fulfilled
  He did not perform miracle as people expected
  He annoyed the listeners when He told them that their forefathers had rejected
 God’s prophets
  He pointed out evils of religious leaders
  They knew Him as the son of Mary and Joseph
  He didn’t fulfill their expectations concerning the Messiah.
